topics.topic: Required test evidence proving that a new placement never reads a conflict copy
questions: What must the Required test observe to prove the invariant that a new placement never reads a conflict copy, rather than only its answer and durable effects?
What must the Required test observe to prove that a new placement never reads a conflict copy, rather than only proving that the call ultimately fails without durable changes?

What must the Required test assert to show that a new placement never reads a conflict copy, since the described refusal and unchanged files can also result from an implementation that reads the file and rejects it afterward?

quotes: - INV-19: delivering content that has no placement under the name of a conflict copy fails with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure, adds no file except the project lock and changes no existing file (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`). Placed content replays when only a conflict copy still holds it (`test_placed_content_replays_when_only_a_conflict_copy_still_holds_it`), and an ordinary file with the content of a conflict copy is delivered (`test_an_ordinary_file_is_placed_when_a_conflict_copy_has_the_same_content`).
judgement.why: The Required tests passage is unchanged from the closed text, and the changes did not create its omission of an observable assertion that the conflict copy was never read.

topics.topic: Required test evidence proving that paths failing condition 1 are never opened
questions: What must the Required test observe to prove that no failing path was opened, rather than only proving the returned failure and durable writes?
What must the Required test observe to prove that delivery opens no path failing condition 1, rather than merely proving the returned failure and absence of durable writes?

What must the test assert to demonstrate the invariant that no path failing A3 rule 5 condition 1 is opened, rather than merely demonstrating the refusal and final durable state, and must it cover the absent-path and unreadable-metadata branches of that condition?

quotes: - INV-02: for content with no placement, an empty or absolute name, a name with an empty, `.` or `..` segment, an ignored name at any level, a folder, and a path through a symbolic link each fail with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure and add no file except the project lock (`test_a_name_a_scan_would_not_report_is_not_delivered`).
judgement.why: The Required tests passage is unchanged from the closed text, and the changes did not create its omission of an assertion that failing paths, including absent and unreadable-metadata cases, were never opened.

topics.topic: Whether path opening must be anchored and reject symbolic links or substitutions in every path component
questions: Does “a path that became a symbolic link” include every ancestor segment as well as the final segment, and must a substitution after the metadata check be refused even when opening through the new link succeeds?

If an intermediate folder is replaced by a symbolic link after condition 1 checks it but before the file is opened, must opening be anchored so that no intermediate link can be followed, and which A1 order and PlacementFailure result apply when that race is detected?

Must opening be anchored to the photo-folder directory and refuse symbolic links in every path component even when a previously checked parent is replaced by a link between metadata checking and opening, or does “without following a link” protect only the final component?

quotes: | 5 | opening or reading it fails, which includes a file that disappeared and a path that became a symbolic link after the listing | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
| 2 | A1 orders 1 to 6 reject the file | `EMPTY` for order 1, `TOO_LARGE` for orders 2 and 4, `NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE` for order 3, `UNREADABLE_FILE` for order 5, `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT` for order 6 |
judgement.why: This is the same directory-anchored traversal and checked-folder substitution question already decided by P4, and its cited passages have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Directory-anchored traversal and result when a checked folder segment is replaced
quotes: | 5 | opening or reading it fails, which includes a file that disappeared and a path that became a symbolic link after the listing | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
| 2 | A1 orders 1 to 6 reject the file | `EMPTY` for order 1, `TOO_LARGE` for orders 2 and 4, `NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE` for order 3, `UNREADABLE_FILE` for order 5, `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT` for order 6 |
precedent.why: A path that becomes symbolic after validation is an A1 order-5 failure, and delivery maps that failure to UNREADABLE_FILE rather than following and placing the outside file.

topics.topic: Scope of INV-01 across metadata fields and refused or failed operation paths
questions: Must the invariant cover source metadata not named here, such as access times, ownership and extended attributes, and must it be shown for refused and failed operation paths as well as the four listed successful actions?

quotes: - INV-01: after a scan, a placement, a repeated placement and a mark, the source folder holds the same files with the same bytes, modification times and modes (`test_no_operation_changes_the_source_folder`).
judgement.why: The Required tests passage is unchanged from the closed text, and the changes did not create its omission of other metadata or refused and failed operation paths.

topics.topic: Whether post-open metadata validation is part of opening and must precede every read
questions: Does A3's phrase "the opening decides" include the metadata reading performed after a successful open, so that failure of that reading or discovery of a non-regular opened object always prevents every read?

quotes:
A file is then opened: an opening that fails, or a failed metadata reading of the opened file,
is order 5, and an opened object that is not a regular file is order 3; either ends the work on that file
before any byte is read.
judgement.why: The passage explicitly makes the post-open metadata reading part of the pre-read decision and requires both its failure and discovery of a non-regular object to end processing before any byte is read.

topics.topic: Whether “read once” means one system call or a complete retrying logical read
questions: Does “read once” mean one operating-system read call or one logical pass that continues after short reads, and are interrupted reads retried or treated as order 5?

quotes:
A file that
changes while it is read is judged by the bytes that were read, once, without a retry.

Otherwise it is read once, up to one byte past the imported `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` constant: reaching
that byte is order 4, and the read stops there. A read that reaches the end of the file with no bytes is
order 1.

metadata is opened, and unless the opening decides A1 order 3 or 5, read once; the bytes that were read
   are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.
| 5 | opening or reading it fails, which includes a file that disappeared and a path that became a symbolic link after the listing | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats “read once” as one logical pass and continues after a positive short system read until EOF or the limit, while another treats the first system-read result as the complete bytes; the caller can see `placed` versus `SOURCE_CHANGED`, and interrupted reads are likewise left open between retry and `UNREADABLE_FILE`.
judgement.why: The texts define the stopping limit and use of the bytes obtained but do not say whether a positive short read continues or whether an interrupted system read is retried.

witness.initial: A regular valid image is smaller than the source limit, its requested source id is the SHA-256 of the complete file, and the first underlying read returns a positive prefix without EOF.
events: The caller requests delivery of the image with its complete-file source id.
The deliverer opens the regular file and the operating system supplies a positive short read.
One implementation continues the same logical pass to EOF; another treats that first result as the completed read.
outcomes: The logical-pass implementation hashes the complete image and can answer `placed`.
The one-system-call implementation hashes only the prefix and answers `SOURCE_CHANGED`.
basis:
3. One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, a relative path in the form a scan reports, and
   `source_id`. The service keeps no memory of earlier scans: it judges the name and the file when the call
   runs. A named file that passes condition 1 of rule 5 and that A1 orders 1 and 2 do not reject from its
   metadata is opened, and unless the opening decides A1 order 3 or 5, read once; the bytes that were read
   are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.
| 3 | the hash of the bytes differs from `source_id` | `SOURCE_CHANGED` |

Otherwise it is read once, up to one byte past the imported `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` constant: reaching
that byte is order 4, and the read stops there. A read that reaches the end of the file with no bytes is
order 1.
